summary: Contestants apply accounting principles to analyze transactions, prepare financial statements, and interpret data to support organizational decision-making. The event is for secondary division students who have not completed their first year of accounting. Contestants demonstrate their skills through an application event with both objective and practical components.
time_limits: No more than ten (10) minutes for orientation
No more than ninety (90) minutes for testing
No more than ten (10) minutes for wrap-up
what_to_bring: Published and/or unpublished non-electronic written reference materials
competencies: Apply the steps of the accounting cycle to accurately process financial transactions and explain their relevance in maintaining organizational financial integrity
Apply the fundamental accounting equation to analyze financial transactions and ensure accuracy in reporting
Apply accounting standards to evaluate and report the value of assets, liabilities, and owner’s equity in accordance with GAAP
Explain key accounting concepts and articulate the role of accounting systems in supporting financial decision-making and organizational accountability
Analyze accruals and deferrals to ensure accurate financial reporting and alignment with accounting principles and timing requirements
Prepare and interpret financial statements and reports to assess organizational performance and support strategic decision-making
Apply adjusting and closing entries to update accounts and ensure accurate period-end financial reporting
Evaluate various forms of business ownership to determine their legal, financial, and operational implications for organizational decision-making
Evaluate the characteristics and operational models of service and merchandising businesses to guide financial practices and strategic decision-making
Analyze purchase and sales transactions for merchandise to ensure accurate recording and inventory management
Evaluate uncollectible accounts to determine appropriate accounting treatment and ensure compliance with financial reporting standards
Apply appropriate depreciation methods to plant assets to ensure accurate financial reporting and compliance with accounting standards
Utilize general and subsidiary ledgers to organize and track detailed financial data, supporting accurate reporting and efficient account management
Apply periodic inventory methods to calculate cost of goods sold and evaluate inventory performance in alignment with accounting standards
Analyze financial performance using key ratios and dashboards, integrating data visualization tools and benchmarking techniques
judging_notes: No equipment, supplies, or materials other than those specified for an event will be allowed in the testing area.

Previous Business Professionals of America tests and/or sample tests or facsimiles (handwritten, photocopied or keyed) may not be taken into the testing area. Violation of this rule will result in disqualification.
AI Policy Level 1 No AI Allowed
eligibility_notes: This application event is limited to secondary division contestants who have not completed their first year of accounting.
Contestants may not enter Fundamental Accounting and Advanced Accounting in the same year.
This event may not be repeated.
